---
title: "Configuration"
---

You configure the app in two files. `form.yml` holds the site settings and the
form fields that users see. `submit.yml.erb` turns the form values into Slurm
options. The scripts under `template/` start Positron Server on the compute
node. This page covers each setting, then the Apptainer, GPU, and license
options.

## Site settings

The site settings are the fixed values at the top of `form.yml`. Users do not
see them. Each one is a string. An empty string turns the setting off.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cluster` | `"hpc"` | The cluster the job is submitted to. It must match a file name in `/etc/ood/config/clusters.d/`, without `.yml`. The default matches the [local validation cluster](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-server-ood/tree/main/dev). |
| `positron_server_dir` | `"/opt/positron-server"` | Directory of a plain Positron Server install. The job adds `<positron_server_dir>/bin` to `PATH`. Leave it empty when `positron-server` is already on `PATH`, or when the module below provides it. |
| `positron_module` | `""` | An environment module to load before the server starts, for example `positron-server/2026.10.0`. The job runs `module load` with this value. |
| `apptainer_image` | `""` | Path to an Apptainer image. When set, the job runs `positron-server` inside this image. See [Run inside Apptainer](#run-inside-apptainer). |
| `apptainer_binds` | `""` | Extra bind mounts for Apptainer, comma separated, for example `/scratch,/project`. Only used when `apptainer_image` is set. |

### Install location {#install-location}

The job finds `positron-server` in this order:

1. If `positron_module` is set, the job loads that module.
2. If `positron_server_dir` is set, the job puts `<positron_server_dir>/bin`
   first on `PATH`.
3. The job runs `positron-server` from `PATH`.

So a site with a module sets `positron_module` and leaves
`positron_server_dir` empty. A site with a shared directory sets
`positron_server_dir`. A site that already has `positron-server` on every
user's `PATH` leaves both empty.

## Form fields

These are the fields that users see when they launch the app. To change a
default, edit the `value` of the field in `form.yml`. To hide a field and fix
its value, replace the whole field entry with a string, for example
`num_gpus: "0"`.

| Field | Label | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `working_dir` | Working directory | user's home | The directory Positron opens. The user picks it with the OOD file picker. A path that does not exist falls back to the home directory. |
| `bc_account` | Account | none | Slurm account, passed as `--account`. With no value, OOD omits the option and Slurm uses the user's default account. |
| `bc_queue` | Partition | none | Slurm partition, passed as `--partition`. With no value, OOD omits the option and Slurm uses the default partition. |
| `bc_num_hours` | Hours | `1` | Wall time in hours. OOD passes it as `--time`. |
| `num_cores` | Cores | `1` | CPU cores. Passed as `--cpus-per-task`. |
| `memory_gb` | Memory (GB) | `2.5` | Memory for the job, in GB. Passed as `--mem` in MB. Positron Server needs at least 2.5 GB. |
| `num_gpus` | GPUs | `0` | Number of GPUs. When above 0, the job adds `--gres=gpu:<n>`. See [GPUs](#gpus). |

`bc_account`, `bc_queue`, and `bc_num_hours` are OOD built-in fields. OOD
turns them into Slurm options itself, and leaves the option out of the job
when the field is blank. The `native` list in `submit.yml.erb` adds the rest:

```{.yaml filename="submit.yml.erb"}
script:
  native:
    - "--nodes=1"
    - "--ntasks=1"
    - "--cpus-per-task=<%= num_cores.blank? ? 1 : num_cores.to_i %>"
    - "--mem=<%= ((memory_gb.blank? ? 2.5 : memory_gb.to_f) * 1024).round %>M"
<%- if num_gpus.to_i > 0 -%>
    - "--gres=gpu:<%= num_gpus.to_i %>"
<%- end -%>
```

Add your own Slurm options to this list. For example, to make every session
use a QOS, add `- "--qos=interactive"`.

### Memory

Allocate memory per session based on the size of the workload:

| Workload | Minimum | Recommended |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| Light: one console, a few extensions, simple scripts | 2 GB | 2.5 GB |
| Standard: several consoles, several extensions, app development | 2.5 GB | 4 GB |
| Heavy: large datasets, language servers, several apps at once | 4 GB | 6 GB or more |

Slurm stops a session that goes over the request. Signs of too little memory
are slow runtime switching, extensions that fail to install, and crashes
during large operations.

## Template variables

The scripts in `template/` read the form values through `context`. They also
set these variables:

| Variable | Set in | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `port` | `before.sh.erb` | A free port on the compute node, from the OOD `find_port` helper. |
| `password` | `before.sh.erb` | A random 32-character connection token. OOD writes it to the session's `connection.yml`, and the Connect button sends it as the `tkn` query parameter. |
| `POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN_FILE` | `before.sh.erb` | Path of the token file, `connection-token` in the session's output directory, mode `600`. Passed to `positron-server` as `--connection-token-file`. |

`script.sh.erb` starts the server with these options:

```{.bash filename="template/script.sh.erb"}
positron-server \
  --host "0.0.0.0" \
  --port "${port}" \
  --connection-token-file "${POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN_FILE}" \
  --accept-server-license-terms \
  --telemetry-level off \
  --disable-workspace-trust \
  --default-folder "<working_dir>"
```

`--disable-workspace-trust` turns off the Code OSS workspace trust prompt.
Without it, Positron opens the working directory in Restricted Mode and
refuses to start a console until the user selects **Trust this folder**.
The user picked the directory and owns the session, so the prompt adds
nothing. Remove the option from `script.sh.erb` to bring the prompt back.

The server keeps its data in `~/.positron-server` for each user. Extensions
and settings persist from one session to the next.

`after.sh` waits up to 600 seconds for the port to open. Raise that number
if your compute nodes are slow to start a job.

## Run inside Apptainer {#run-inside-apptainer}

Set `apptainer_image` to run Positron Server from an Apptainer image instead
of a host install. The job then runs:

```{.bash filename="template/script.sh.erb"}
apptainer exec --bind "${BINDS}" "<apptainer_image>" positron-server ...
```

`BINDS` is the session output directory, `TMPDIR` when it is set, and the
value of `apptainer_binds`. Apptainer binds the home directory by default.
Add any other filesystem the user needs, such as scratch or project space,
to `apptainer_binds`.

The image must have `positron-server` on `PATH`, or `positron_server_dir`
must point at the install inside the image. The job passes
`positron_server_dir/bin` to Apptainer through `APPTAINERENV_PREPEND_PATH`.

This is an example definition file that unpacks the CDN archive and places
the license file. Replace `<arch>` with `x86_64` or `aarch64`, and put
`license.lic` next to the definition file before you build.

```{.text filename="positron-server.def"}
Bootstrap: docker
From: rockylinux/rockylinux:9

%files
    license.lic /opt/license.lic

%post
    dnf install -y tar gzip
    mkdir -p /opt/positron-server
    CDN=https://cdn.posit.co/positron/releases/server
    curl -L "$CDN/x86_64/positron-server-linux-x64-{{< var positron.version >}}.tar.gz" \
      | tar -xz -C /opt/positron-server --strip-components=1
    install -m 644 /opt/license.lic \
      /opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic
    rm /opt/license.lic

%environment
    export PATH=/opt/positron-server/bin:$PATH
```

Build it with `apptainer build positron-server.sif positron-server.def`.
Install R and Python into the image as well, or bind them in from the host,
because the consoles inside Positron use the interpreters that the server
process can see.

::: callout-note
Confirm with Posit whether your Positron Server build should run inside a
container. The example definition is untested against a production site, and
the command and bind list are the only parts this app controls.
:::

## GPUs {#gpus}

When a user requests one or more GPUs:

- `submit.yml.erb` adds `--gres=gpu:<n>` to the Slurm job.
- With Apptainer, `script.sh.erb` adds `--nv` to `apptainer exec`, so the
  NVIDIA driver and libraries from the host are visible inside the image.

Positron Server itself does not use a GPU. The GPU is for the R and Python
code that users run in the session. If your cluster has no GPUs, hide the
field by setting `num_gpus: "0"` in `form.yml`.

## License file location {#license-file-location}

`positron-server` looks for a license in this order and uses the first one
that validates:

1. The `--license-key` and `--license-key-file` command-line options.
2. The `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY` and `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` environment
   variables.
3. A `license-key` file in the user data directory.
4. A `.lic` file in the activation directory,
   `<install>/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/`.

The first three are for signed per-session keys, which a product such as
Posit Workbench mints. The app does not set any of them. The license file
from Posit goes in the activation directory, item 4, as
[Get started](get_started.qmd#place-the-license-file) describes.

If the install directory is read-only, or the same install serves several
clusters, you have two options:

- With Apptainer, bind the file to the exact path inside the image. Add
  `/path/to/license.lic:/opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic:ro`
  to `apptainer_binds`.
- Without Apptainer, set `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` to the path of
  `license.lic` in `script.sh.erb`, before the server starts. On Positron
  Server 2026.09.0 and newer, this variable accepts a raw `license.lic`.
  The server then copies the file into the activation directory, so the
  directory must be writable by the first session that starts. On a
  read-only install, use the Apptainer bind instead.
